records.name: Philly Peace in Progress
records.summary: A West Philadelphia nonprofit that offers mentoring, tutoring, food help and life skills to youth, families and older adults, with a focus on young people affected by violence.
records.what_you_do: Pick a program from the Get Help page, or call to ask which one fits. Services run at partner sites such as recreation centers and libraries. Volunteers sign up through a form on the Volunteer page, which lists about 40 roles from event helpers to youth mentors and grant writers.

schedule.text: Office hours are Tuesday to Thursday, 4:00 to 7:30 pm. Programs run at partner sites, so each program sets its own days and times.

locations.label: West Philadelphia, at partner sites such as recreation centers and libraries

cost.text: Food giveaways are free. PJ and Pages costs $20 per child per year. Career coaching asks for a small donation when possible. The site gives no fee for other programs.

first_step.how: Call (445) 208-0177, use the Contact Now button or the form on the Contact page to ask which program fits, or use the Sign Up to Volunteer form on the Volunteer page.
first_step.basis: Programs are open to the public, and the site gives a phone number, a contact form and a sign-up route for volunteers. It does not say whether walk-ins are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: The page does not describe a first visit. Programs meet at partner sites, so the place and time depend on the program, and the office keeps hours on Tuesday to Thursday, 4:00 to 7:30 pm. Food giveaways are free, and the group also holds events such as a 2026 holiday event for families.
first_visit_tips: Call (445) 208-0177 before you go to ask which program fits.
Ask whether walk-ins are welcome, since the page does not say.
Check the Events page, but note that many listed events do not print a date.

records.notes: Status is active on year-only 2026 evidence (a 2026 holiday event listing and a 2026 impact statement with no month), so last_sign_of_life is left out. Office hours are not program hours. The volunteer page says nothing about background checks, even though several volunteer roles work with youth. The mailing address, P.O. Box 13250, Philadelphia, PA 19104, is on the contact page and was not recorded as a location.

records.name: Belles and Chimes Philly
records.summary: A pinball league for women players that meets at Barcade Fishtown on the second Tuesday of each month. Players sign in at a sheet at the venue, play league games, and join the group's tournaments.
records.what_you_do: Sign in at the league sheet at the venue, play league nights each month, and enter the group's tournaments, which have included summer, spooky season and winter events.

schedule.text: Second Tuesday of each month at Barcade Fishtown. Sign-ups begin around 7:30 pm and games start shortly after 8 pm.

cost.text: Each game costs 3 tokens, and a night has 5 games, according to the January 2026 newsletter. No membership or entry fee is mentioned. The price of a token is not stated.

first_step.how: Go to Barcade Fishtown on the second Tuesday. Sign in at the league sheet from about 7:30 pm, and games start shortly after 8 pm. You can join at any league night.
first_step.basis: The January 2026 newsletter says all skill levels are welcome, mentions people who have never joined before, and explains how to sign in at the venue. No orientation or buddy program is described.
first_step.what_to_expect: League nights start with the sign-in sheet from about 7:30 pm, and games start shortly after 8 pm. Each game costs 3 tokens and a night has 5 games, so plan on paying for tokens. The group also holds tournaments, and its newsletter says players of all skill levels are welcome.
first_visit_tips: Arrive around 7:30 pm to get on the sign-in sheet before games start.
Plan for token costs: 3 tokens per game and 5 games per night.
Watch the newsletter for the next league night and tournament news.

records.notes: Tier 1 merged two leagues. This record is Belles and Chimes Philly: a women's league on the second Tuesday. Philly Pinball Club is a separate Monday league at Barcade Fishtown with its own newsletter (see leads_only), so the aka Philly Pinball Club should come off this record. Last sign of life 2026-07 comes from the Philly Pinball Club newsletter of 2026-07-27, which says the next Belles and Chimes meeting is Tuesday, August 11. The Belles post itself does not say whether players must be women; the Philly Pinball Club post calls Belles an inclusive women's league and a flyer caption calls it a women's league.

records.name: Philly Revolution
records.summary: An AAU basketball club with tryouts for boys and girls in grades 4 to 11, plus camps and clinics for younger players in grades 1 to 8.
records.what_you_do: Players register through the online forms on the site, pick Boys or Girls and a grade, and pay the fee. The club runs weekly camps and one-day and two-day clinics at gyms it lists, one in Philadelphia and two outside the city.

schedule.text: Weekly camps and one-day or two-day clinics run at the listed gyms. The site does not post session dates or times.

cost.text: Tryouts cost $10 for grade school teams and $20 for high school teams, paid at tryout. One-day clinics are $70, two-day clinics are $100, and a weekly camp is $175. Camp and clinic fees can be paid by Venmo, or in cash or by check at the door.

first_step.how: Fill out the online 2027 tryout form on the Tryouts page, or the camp and clinic form for a session. Choose Boys or Girls and the grade, then pay the fee.
first_step.basis: Camps and clinics take online registration with listed prices, so a newcomer can join without a tryout. Team places come through 2027 tryouts, and the site does not explain what tryouts involve.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a session day, the coaches or start times. The registration forms ask for the player's grade and school, and a parent's name, phone and email. Tryouts cost $10 or $20, and camps and clinics cost $70 to $175.
first_visit_tips: Register online before the session, with a parent's phone and email ready, since the forms ask for them.
Ask which gym hosts your session, since the site does not say which gym hosts which session.
Pay by Venmo to @PhillyRevHoops with the player's name and session in the memo, or bring cash or a check to the door.

records.notes: The only dated item is a Presidents Day Clinic on February 16, 2026 at John Marynowitz Gym, listed on the camps page; status is active on that basis. Team entry is through 2027 tryouts, and the page does not say what tryouts involve or what the grade school and high school cut-offs are. The home page photo is labelled 2027 girls, but the forms offer Boys or Girls, so do not assume the teams are girls only. The email address is hidden on the site and no phone number is listed. Two of the three gyms are outside Philadelphia, and the page does not say which session uses which gym.

records.name: Philly Sensory Theatre
records.summary: Makes original, inclusive, immersive live theatre for families. Its current show, Quack Quack Philly! A Sensory Musical, follows a duck that gets lost after a river flood and travels across Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to a show. Each audience member gets a bag of props to use during the show.

schedule.text: Show dates are listed by each venue and on the group's Eventbrite page. The group's own site does not list dates.

cost.text: Ticket prices are not listed on the group's site. Each show's listing gives the price.

first_step.how: Open the Free Library calendar listing or the Upper Darby Arts Education Foundation listing for Quack Quack Philly!, both linked from phillysensorytheatre.org, and choose a show date.
first_step.basis: Shows are open to the public and listed at public venues. The group's site describes no other steps to attend.
first_step.what_to_expect: Quack Quack Philly! is a sensory musical for families, and each audience member gets a bag of props to use during the show. The group's site does not print dates, venues or run times for the current show, so check each listing.
first_visit_tips: Check the listing for the show date, venue and ticket price before you go.
Ask the venue about accessibility before the show, since the group's site does not list ASL, captioning or sensory-friendly performances.

records.notes: Dates, venues and prices for the current show live on external listings that could not be read. The two Free Library event pages returned HTTP 403 and were not retried, and the Free Library listing for Quack Quack Philly! was not opened for the same reason. The Upper Darby listing was not opened. Status is active on year-only evidence: the productions menu lists Light Years Away 2026, with no month, so last_sign_of_life is left out. The Instagram handle and the Eventbrite organizer page use the name Philly Children's Theatre. A search summary said that is a separate group founded in 2021, but this was not verified, so check whether the two names are one group before publishing. No access details (ASL, captioning, sensory-friendly performances) appear on any page read. A search summary claimed ages 1 to 8 and no-shush shows, but no page read confirmed it, so it is not recorded.

records.name: Philly Voice For Change
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that works to keep families together when poverty, substance use or contact with public systems puts them at risk. Its team has social workers, attorneys, peer mentors and people with lived experience of the system.
records.what_you_do: Reach out through the contact form on the website, or by email or phone, to ask about getting involved or partnering. The group builds coalitions and offers mentorship, advocacy and direct support, and it names partners such as JMAC For Families and Temple Legal Aid Office. The site does not describe a volunteer schedule or an intake process.

locations.label: Office
locations.address: 100 South Broad Street, Suite 660, Philadelphia, PA 19110

first_step.how: Use the contact form on phillyvoiceforchange.org, or call 215-449-0202 or email info@thephillyvoice.org, to ask how to get involved or partner with the group.
first_step.basis: The site invites people to get involved or partner, and it offers a contact form and an update signup. It does not describe volunteer roles, intake steps or what happens after you reach out.
first_step.what_to_expect: The page does not describe a first visit or an intake step. Reaching out starts with the contact form, email or phone. The office is at 100 South Broad Street, Suite 660, and the page lists no office hours.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-449-0202 or email before you visit, since the site lists no office hours.
Have your name and email ready, since the contact form requires an email address.
Note how you heard about the group, because the form asks.

records.notes: The home page summary mentions sending referrals, but the contact page does not, so the record does not promise a referral route. Partners named on the site without links: JMAC For Families and Temple Legal Aid Office. No office hours are posted. The footer reads Copyright 2024, which is not evidence of activity. No dated event or news item was found, so the status stays probably active.

records.name: Philly Youth Inc.
records.summary: A Philadelphia youth development group. It runs a youth program with self-care, book club discussions and leadership, a monthly virtual book club, a feature that shares young people's stories, and trips abroad for teens.
records.what_you_do: Teens ages 12 to 17 can register for the youth program, which covers self-care, book club discussions, leadership, college and career readiness, and travel. Teens ages 13 to 17 can join the monthly virtual book club. Young people can apply to be featured in the Top Influencers stories, which the feature page says is for ages 25 and under. Volunteers can help with travel recruiting, the app, outreach, fundraising or marketing.

schedule.text: The virtual book club meets online once a month. The site gives no meeting days or times.

cost.text: The site lists no program fees. Donations help pay for trips, cultural activities and scholarships for teens who need help to take part. The book club page does not say whether donating is required to join.

first_step.how: Sign up for the youth program through the Register Today form on the Events page, or for the virtual book club through the sign-up form on its page. Email info@phillyyouthinc.com with questions.
first_step.basis: The youth program and the book club both have open online sign-up forms with no tryout or approval step listed. The site does not describe what a meeting is like or give meeting times.
first_step.what_to_expect: After you sign up for the virtual book club, you get a welcome kit with the book of the month and login details. Meetings are online once a month, with a facilitator, discussion of the book and challenges tied to it. The site gives no meeting times and no fee for the book club.
first_visit_tips: Read the month's book before the online meeting, since the discussion is about the book.
Have a device with internet access for the online meetings.
Ask whether donating is required to join, since the book club page does not say.

records.notes: The home page says the Top Influencers feature is for ages 12 to 25 and applies through a form, but the feature page says 25 and under and asks people to email. This record uses the feature page wording and lists both routes in what_you_do. The 21 and under limit on the volunteer page applies to youth a travel recruiter signs up, not to volunteers. Volunteer age limits, time commitment and background checks are not stated. Self-Care Saturdays has no details beyond its name and a short description. The travel plans named are tours to London and Paris, with a GoFundMe and no dates. The Philly Youth app is listed for iPhone and Android.

records.name: PhillyMesh (Philly Mesh)
records.summary: Hobbyists who build and run Meshtastic and MeshCore radio nodes across the Philadelphia area, and who share how-to guides for newcomers. They also experiment with AREDN mesh networks.
records.what_you_do: Join the Philly Radio and Mesh Discord to ask questions and meet local people, follow the Getting Started guides to set up a node, and try mesh experiments with other members. Local meetups are announced in the Discord.

schedule.text: No regular meeting is listed. The 2025 Getting Started guide says local meetups happen a few times a year and are announced in the Discord's meetups channel. The same guide says Iffy Books hosts Meshtastic 101 events on a regular basis.

cost.text: No membership fee is mentioned. Radio hardware is an extra cost, and the guide suggests starting with an inexpensive device.

first_step.how: Join the Philly Radio and Mesh Discord, with the invite link on phillymesh.net, then start with the Getting Started guide and ask questions in the chat.
first_step.basis: The Getting Started guide is written for people setting up their first node and gives step-by-step starts, and the MeshCore intro is aimed at people new to it. The public Discord is open to chat. The site does not say that meetups welcome newcomers.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most of the activity happens in the Discord, where local Meshtastic and MeshCore users answer questions. The guide walks you through a cheap starter node set up by a window for several hours, then a battery node later. The site lists no membership fee, but you will need to buy radio hardware.
first_visit_tips: Read the Getting Started guide first, and check its date, since the guide says some parts may be out of date.
Ask questions in the Discord before you buy hardware.
Watch the Discord meetups channel for the next local event.

records.notes: The Getting Started guide is dated June 2025 and says some figures and antenna advice may be out of date. Meetup hosts it names, DC215 and Iffy Books, have no links seen, so they are not in leads_only. The calendar feed is the posts RSS feed, not an events feed. The Discord invite is recorded under social. The group also lists a GitHub organization, which was not recorded as a contact.

notes: Budget: 1 of 1 WebSearch used. 28 WebFetch calls used, within the limit of 6 per group. Two Free Library pages returned HTTP 403 and were recorded as blocked. No rate limiting was seen. Verdicts: 7 publish. Key findings: (1) Tier 1 merged two different leagues under this batch id. Belles and Chimes Philly (women's league, second Tuesday) is the record here. Philly Pinball Club, a separate Monday league at Barcade Fishtown with $20 season dues and a free first night for newcomers, is in leads_only and needs its own record and a decision on the id and aka. (2) Philly Sensory Theatre's Instagram and Eventbrite use the name Philly Children's Theatre. A search summary called that a separate 2021 group. This is unverified, so check before publishing. (3) Philly Youth Inc. gives two different Top Influencers ages and application routes across its home page and feature page. The feature page wording is used. (4) Philly Voice's home page mentions referrals, but its contact page does not. The record avoids promising referrals. (5) Philly Revolution's only dated item is a February 16, 2026 clinic, and two of its three gyms are outside Philadelphia. Status: Philly Peace in Progress and Philly Sensory Theatre are active on year-only 2026 evidence, so their last_sign_of_life is left out because no month was printed. Partner organizations named without links, so not in leads_only: JMAC For Families and Temple Legal Aid Office (Philly Voice); DC215 and Iffy Books (PhillyMesh, from a 2025 guide); and the Upper Darby Arts Education Foundation (a listing host for the Sensory show, reached only through a ticket page).
